messages:
alex: heads up — seeing a noticeable p99 decode latency jump on canary since the merge that landed ~09:10 UTC. p99 up ~25% on 2048-seqlen workloads. :alarm_clock:
riley: ugh, which merge/PR? any CI alerts? :eyes:
perf-bot: Perf CI: tail_latency_p99 increased by 12.4% vs baseline on commit 3f8b2a4 (PR #2345). Link: https://ci.internal/reports/2345
alex: PR #2345 is the kernel selector heuristic refactor (sam authored). It changed the cost model and added a fallback score. I repro locally with a microbenchmark — decode timeouts, can share run log:
```
# bench-decode --model llama-2 --seq 2048 --batch 1
p90: 380ms
p95: 560ms
p99: 1.2s  <-- baseline was ~950ms
allocs increased, trace shows more kernel_fallback calls
```
sam: thanks for flagging. I added the new fallback path to prefer numerically stable kernels; shouldn't be that much slower. Did we maybe regress continuous batching interaction?
nora: I profiled a canary and saw repeated small kernel launches instead of the fused attention path. nvprof shows kernel_selector choosing "attn_generic" instead of "attn_fused_4x" for many batches. Might be the scoring weights changed.
riley: can you paste the selector decision trace? even a single example line helps.
nora: sure — excerpt:
```
selector: sequence_len=1024, batch=1, kv_cache=true -> score(attn_fused_4x)=0.72, score(attn_generic)=0.74 -> chosen: attn_generic
invocation: fallback_count++
```
alex: so it's consistently choosing the slightly higher score generic kernel which is ~30% slower for these shapes. That explains p99 tail.
sam: ah — I changed the latency estimate to include kernel launch overhead but I forgot to account for amortization when batching/kvcache is hot. The cost model now slightly favors the generic implementation in many cases.
riley: can we bisect to confirm 3f8b2a4 is the culprit? perf-bot already pointed at it but we should be sure.
sam: I ran a quick git bisect on the benchmark branch; confirmed the regression lands at 3f8b2a4 (the selector PR). I have a demo revert ready: PR #2350.
alex: patch looks good. Do we want a revert or a targeted fix to the scoring weights? Revert is fastest for rollback to stable canary.
nora: targeted fix would be to add a small heuristic: if kv_cache==true and batch_size<=4 prefer fused when delta_score < 0.05. Quick check locally: applying that heuristic brings p99 back to 980ms.
sam: I'll open a hotfix PR with the threshold and add unit tests for selector decisions. If CI is green we can deploy. Otherwise revert.
perf-bot: Canary check queued for PR #2351 (selector hotfix).
deploy-bot: Rolling canary paused for model-serving rollout due to perf alert (blocking).
riley: thanks, team. Action items: sam push hotfix PR (inflight), alex run canary perf windows on PR, nora add selector unit test and microbench. Hold full rollout until resolution.
alex: assigned tasks. Will run canary checks as soon as PR lands.
sam: PR #2351 opened: fixes scoring and adds heuristic for kv_cache + small batch. PTAL.
perf-bot: PR #2351 bench results: p99 delta = +1.1% vs baseline (within noise).
alex: merging hotfix after review. Reopening rollout blocked but will proceed once CI canary confirms stable for 2 hours. :thumbsup:
riley: excellent, please follow up with a short blurb in the release notes about selector tuning so ops knows why we reverted/change behavior.
nora: will do. Also logging improvement so we can see selector rationale in prod traces.
sam: sorry about the noisefloor on that refactor — will be more conservative with cost-model changes.
alex: thanks everyone. closing thread once canary stable.
